newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds rally on job data, shorts stymied by TWI.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds rally on job data, shorts stymied by TWI.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.96 (PREV 92.99) 90-DAYS 6.78 (PREV 6.78)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.10 PCT (PREV 6.00) US 5-YR 6.53 (PREV 6.51)
* NZ long bonds rally eight basis points at close
* 90-day bank bills held flat by drop in TWI after HLFS data
* U.S. seen dominating local bonds at Wednesday's open
New Zealand long bonds rallied eight basis points on good volume at Tuesday's close as the market took heart from data providing a benign longer term view of inflation.
The 11/06 bond ended at 7.66 percent, while the 02/00 maturity was also lower in yield, down two basis points to 7.34 percent.

Short term interest rates ralllied initially on the back of March quarter employment data from Statistics New Zealand (SNZ), but a falling currency soon put paid to the strength and rates bounced back up to end flat at 6.78 percent.
The currency's Trade Weighted Index finished down at 68.19 percent, from 68.47 percent at Monday's close, after SNZ said employment growth was negative 0.1 percent in the March quarter.
Unemployment rose to 6.4 percent from 5.9 percent in the December quarter.
Dealers said the data confirmed the market's recent easing bias and traders were increasingly confident the Reserve Bank would take an easing stance in its June monetary policy statement.

The data was seen adding to recent figures portraying a soft economy, heightening beliefs that rates' recent move lower will prove sustainable. Bonds had gained from the improved long term view for inflation.
A Wellington dealer said bonds found buying interest in the session that was unrelated to the employment data.
"Also the trader market has been caught short in long bonds," he added. He saw Wednesday's open being dictated largely by the performance of U.S. Treasuries overnight.
"We will be dominated by the U.S. -- that's probably the single most dominant factor in our market at the moment."
-- Catherine McCaw, Wellington newsroom (64 4) 471 4275
